## Contract review brief — PR #37122 @ `fa749f9d3bd041b8fb6e722f2cc10418b47bca6e` (card #37057)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #37057: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #37122: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `fa749f9d3bd041b8fb6e722f2cc10418b47bca6e`
  · the check-runs on `fa749f9d3bd041b8fb6e722f2cc10418b47bca6e`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

Security — if a `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**` and the change teaches security, auth or permission
  behaviour the path name doesn't show, the record says so and the seat adopting the record adds the `security` label.
  The record says so on its `Security-touching:` line, and the arm lands on `no` alone: write `no` ONLY when no changed
  hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token, authentication or other security behaviour, else `yes`.

Rule change — if a `hits` path is under `.claude/**`: the PR body declares `Rule-change:` and you verify it against the diff.
  Write `Rule-change-verified: none` ONLY when no changed hunk alters what an agent may do without the maintainer
  (merge, bypass a check, change repository settings), what gets done and in what order (grading, dispatch, scope), or
  what must go to him (decisions, maintainer actions); process steps, scripts, wording, slimming and file moves are not rule
  changes. Write `ruled` ONLY when every such hunk copies the ruling the PR body quotes on its `Ruling-ref:` line — check the
  copy against the quoted words, do not re-rule it. Otherwise `yes`: the pull request then waits for the maintainer.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-objectstack/177ababb-cccd-573a-a846-cda17d8e5bbd/scratchpad/pr-37122/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fa749f9d3bd041b8fb6e722f2cc10418b47bca6e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md + none
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

### ① Derived judgments

PR #37122, card #37057 item 1 only (`Refs #37057 (item 1)`; item 2 is not in this PR and its absence is not graded). Read: the card body and its 4 comments, the PR body, file list and net diff against `main` (2 files: the skill file and one changeset; merge base `b49a264a10`, and `main` has not moved any file read below since), and the 44 check-runs on the head.

- Accept set: no change. No schema, validator or runtime file is in the diff; the three edited `os:check` blocks lose optional keys only. Right.
- Published surface: one shipped skill file, `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md` (2 sentences rewritten, 3 example lines removed). Right for a `@objectstack/skills` text fix.
- Token ratchet: no ceiling moved and `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` is not in the diff. Blob sizes read off the two trees: 15519 bytes on `main`, 15514 on the head, so ceil(15514 / 4) = 3879 against the row's 3880. The new words are paid by same-file deletion, the discipline's first rule; the standing ruling's raise path (record 6513306068) is not used and need not be. Right.
- Security line: no changed line teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour. The changed lines are the scope of a lint reference check on button names, what an unmatched name draws, and three removed copy and icon keys. `capabilities: ['api.write']` in the Add to Campaign block is unchanged context. `no`.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/37057-actionlayout-validate-scope.md` is `'@objectstack/skills': patch`: right for wording in a published skill with no accept-set change. `Clause-②: no` on the PR body and the changeset: right, nothing is narrowed. `Metadata-protocol: none`: right. Check Changeset is `success` on the head. If the fix of S1 puts a removed line back, the changeset's last sentence (which names the three removed lines) has to follow.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on the head: 28 `success`, 16 `skipped`, none failed, cancelled or pending. The skips are the lanes a skills-only diff does not reach or that are opt-in: the UI lanes (Build and E2E UI, Lint UI, Type Check UI, Build UI Deps, Plan Test UI shards, the Test UI shard matrix, UI Published Artifacts), the Dogfood Regression shard matrix, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Build Docs, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in), 18.x upgrade harness (opt-in), Queue verdict, Borrowed queue verdict, Schedule gate. Every skip is an expected one.
- Dev deviation, four dist-reading gates not run locally: answered by the head's check-runs, all `success` or an expected skip.
- Dev deviation, the paying cuts are example lines and not prose: judged in ④ (S1, N2).
- Dev deviations on MCP reads and the commit trailer: process notes, no effect on the tree.
- `open_questions`: empty.
- Out-of-scope finding, item 2 of the card: the PR body says `Refs`, the card stays open for it. Agreed.
- Out-of-scope finding, the ratchet row comment still spells 15519 bytes: true, and the row could be lowered to 3879 (lowering is always legitimate). Not owed by this PR; the script is outside its claim.
- SQL push-down: no code in the diff; nothing to judge.

### ④ Design judgment

`skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md`, read against `packages/lint/src/validate-object-action-layout.ts` and its test, `ui/packages/types/src/ui-action.ts` (`arrangedHeaderActions`), `packages/objectql/src/registry-custom-arrangement.ts` (`applyCustomArrangement`), `packages/spec/src/data/object-action-layout.ts`, and `skills/objectstack-ui/evals/**`, all on `main`.

(a) The two sentences.

- "`os validate` refuses a name the arm's scope does not place, on the object or an extension of one the same stack defines." Holds, and is exactly the validator's scope: `validateObjectActionLayout` judges each object's own `actionLayout`, then each `objectExtensions` entry only when its `extend` names an entry of the stack's `objects` (lines 149 to 159). The test "judges an extension against the object it extends, and skips one whose object the stack does not define" pins both halves (`crm_lead` judged, `sys_user` skipped).
- "... not judged there: a wrong name draws nothing." Holds. The validator skips that extension; the rule is registered CLI-only (`surfaces: ['cli']`), so the runtime publish door does not judge the names either (the validator's docblock says why); `applyCustomArrangement` replaces the arm whole and reads no name; `arrangedHeaderActions` never looks up a name that matches none of the header's actions (docblock: "is skipped: it draws nothing", pinned by the test "a name naming no placed action, or a `$` built-in, draws nothing").
- N1 (nit) — "not judged there" hangs after "each arm whole" with no subject, and "there" has two candidate antecedents (the `.custom` extension, or `os validate` from the sentence before). Both readings give the same true statement, so no reader is led to a false one. "Not judged" is about names only: the shape (three pinned, a name twice, a `$` built-in) is still refused in an extension by the schema at every door; the colon clause limits it to names in context. Leave, or tighten when the hunk is next touched.

(b) The three example lines removed to pay for it.

- S1 (should-fix) — the Convert Lead `successMessage` cut leaves the skill disagreeing with its own eval. `skills/objectstack-ui/evals/views-apps-actions-pages.json` case 3 is the scenario these two blocks answer (a Convert action on `lead` plus a bulk Add to campaign). Its `expected_output` lists, for Convert, "`confirmText`, `successMessage`, `refreshAfter: true`", and its `must_contain` holds `successMessage`. The prompt asks for no toast, so an answer carries the key only by following the examples; on `main` both blocks carry it, on this head neither does. What still teaches the key is the `successMessage` / `errorMessage` bullet and the Reassign Lead block, a different action. So the token is not untaught, but in the scenario the case scores, both lines that put it in the answer are gone and the expected answer now names a key the worked example lacks. No check-run on the head is an eval run, so green CI does not answer this; the regression is read, not measured (read-only round). Fix, one of: (1) put `successMessage` back on the Convert Lead block and pay those bytes elsewhere in this file (the file is at 15514 bytes and the row allows 15520); or (2) keep the cut and bring case 3 in line in this PR (its `expected_output` and its `must_contain`), which removes an assertion and is the seat's call, not the dev's. (1) is preferred.
- N2 (nit) — after the cut no block shows `successMessage` beside `onSuccess` on one action. The schema accepts both (the `os:check` block carried both on `main`), no sentence in the file says one excludes the other, and the only exclusion the file teaches is `resultDialog`'s. Nothing wrong is taught; fix (1) of S1 restores the one demonstration.
- Add to Campaign `icon`: no loss. Convert Lead still spells `icon: 'arrow-right-circle'`, and no eval token depends on an action's `icon` (`record-page.json` case 2's `icon` is the list's hover icon, taught in `record-page.md` and `SKILL.md`).
- Add to Campaign `successMessage`: the key's spelling and holes are still shown (Reassign Lead block, the bullet, the copy-holes bullet). Its only cost is the one S1 names.
- Is cutting example keys "restatement" under the standing rule: the question does not arise on this PR. Restatement is what the raise path of record 6513306068 asks for; with no ceiling raised, genuine same-file deletion is all the ratchet requires, and the dev's report says honestly that no prose restatement was left. The PR body's "repeat a key another example already shows" is accurate as to spelling; S1 is what those lines carried beyond spelling.

One should-fix (S1), no must-fix. S1 is open on this head; its fix earns a delta review.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e799ec7699f992189593aff0304564040ac53e47`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md + none
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

This is a DELTA record over the earlier one on this PR (record 7144254679: PASS at head fa749f9d3b, should-fix S1, nits N1 and N2). It judges what the one commit since then changed and re-reads the gates on the new head; everything that record judged and this one does not name again is unchanged and stands.

### ① Derived judgments

PR #37122, card #37057 item 1 only (`Refs #37057 (item 1)`; item 2 is not in this PR and its absence is not graded). Read: the prior record and its brief, the PR body, the net diff against `main` at this head, the delta commit `e799ec7699` on its own, and the 48 check-runs on this head.

- The delta: one commit on top of the reviewed head, no merge of `main`. It touches the skill file (2 lines added, 2 removed) and the changeset (its last sentence). The net diff against `main` is still 2 files: the skill file (5 lines added, 6 removed) and the changeset (10 added). `main` is 4 commits past the merge base `b49a264a10`; none of them touches `skills/objectstack-ui/**` or the ratchet script.
- Accept set: no change. No schema, validator or runtime file is in the diff; the edited `os:check` block loses optional keys only. Right.
- Published surface: the one shipped skill file. Against `main` it now differs by: two sentences rewritten under "Button Order (`actionLayout`)" (unchanged since the prior head), three lines removed from the Add to Campaign example (`icon: 'send'`, `successMessage: 'Leads added to campaign!'`, `refreshAfter: true`), and the gloss " (the handler's answer)" removed from the copy-holes bullet. The Convert Lead block is byte-identical to `main`. Right for a `@objectstack/skills` text fix.
- Token ratchet: the blob is 15519 bytes on `main` and 15519 bytes on this head (107 bytes added, 107 removed), so ceil(15519 / 4) = 3880 against the row's 3880, headroom 0: at the ceiling, not over it. `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` is not in the diff and is the same blob on `main` and on this head, so no ceiling moved. The new words are paid by same-file deletion; the raise path of the standing ruling is not used. Right.
- Security line, judged again on the net diff: no changed line teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour. The changed lines are the scope of a lint reference check on button names, what an unmatched name draws, three removed example keys (an icon, a toast sentence, a refresh flag) and one removed gloss on a copy hole. `capabilities: ['api.write']` beside the removed lines is unchanged context. `no`.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/37057-actionlayout-validate-scope.md` is `'@objectstack/skills': patch`: right for wording in a published skill with no accept-set change. `Clause-②: no` on the PR body and the changeset: right, nothing is narrowed. `Metadata-protocol: none`: right. Check Changeset is `success` on this head (both of its runs).

The changeset's last sentence now names what the diff removes: three Add to Campaign example lines (`icon`, `successMessage`, `refreshAfter`) and the gloss "(the handler's answer)" on the copy-holes bullet. That is the net removal against `main`, item for item, and the Convert Lead `successMessage` is no longer named. Its clause "which the `resultDialog` bullet above it already says" is loose (that bullet says the dialog shows "the server answer" and reads `result.data`; it does not speak of copy holes), see N3; it claims nothing untrue.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on this head: 48, all completed; 30 `success`, 18 `skipped`, none with any other conclusion. Four more than on the prior head: the PR-event workflows ran a second time when the PR body was edited (PR-body guards `success`, Check Changeset `success`, Auto Label `skipped`, Check PR Size `skipped`), and Auto Label and Check PR Size each also have a `success` run on this head. The other 16 skips are the same lanes as before, the ones a skills-only diff does not reach or that are opt-in: Build and E2E UI, Lint UI, Type Check UI, Build UI Deps, Plan Test UI shards, the Test UI shard matrix, UI Published Artifacts, the Dogfood Regression shard matrix, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Build Docs, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in), 18.x upgrade harness (opt-in), Queue verdict, Borrowed queue verdict, Schedule gate. Every skip is an expected one.
- Dev note, the PR body's readings table: 267 lines, 15519 bytes and 3880 tokens after, read off the head's blob; the "107 bytes" of cuts is 16 + 46 + 22 + 23, counted off the removed text. Both hold.
- Dev note, N1 left as is: accepted. The file has no byte to spare and both readings of "not judged there" are true.
- Dev note, the four dist-reading gates not measured locally at the prior head: answered by this head's check-runs.
- `open_questions`: none.
- Out-of-scope, item 2 of the card: unchanged, the PR says `Refs` and the card stays open for it.
- SQL push-down: no code in the diff; nothing to judge.

### ④ Design judgment

`skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md` at this head, read against `skills/objectstack-ui/evals/**`, `packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts` (`refreshAfter`, `successMessage`, `outcomeMessages`, `onSuccess.navigate`), `ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx` (`runBulkActionRecord`, `handleBulkDialogClose`) and `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx`, all on `main`.

- S1: closed. The Convert Lead block again carries `successMessage: 'Lead converted successfully!',` (line 100, between `confirmText` and `onSuccess`), and the whole block compares equal to `main`'s byte for byte; the net diff against `main` has no hunk in it. Case 3 of `views-apps-actions-pages.json` lists `confirmText`, `successMessage` and `refreshAfter: true` for Convert and holds `successMessage` in `must_contain`: all three are on the worked example again. N2 goes with it: one block again shows `successMessage` beside `onSuccess`.

- The `refreshAfter: true` cut on the Add to Campaign example: no finding.
  - What the file teaches about the key is its closing line, "Set `refreshAfter: true` whenever the action mutates the current record", untouched. This body inserts a `campaign_member` row (`lead_id: ctx.recordId`) and writes no lead, so by the file's own rule the example never owed the key.
  - The block declares no `locations`; by the file's second paragraph it is reached only through a view's `bulkActions`. On that path the list is re-read when the bulk dialog closes with at least one row succeeded, and that code does not consult `refreshAfter` (`handleBulkDialogClose`); `runBulkActionRecord` passes nothing of the runner's `reload` answer on. So with or without the line the list is re-read once the run ends.
  - The key is still shown where it does something: Convert Lead (line 102, a flow that changes the lead) and Add Line (line 258, a child insert from the record header, where `refreshAfter: true` is what re-reads the page's related lists). An author looking for "child insert, do I refresh" still finds Add Line.
  - Evals: no `must_contain` anywhere under `skills/objectstack-ui/evals/**` holds `refreshAfter`. It appears in two `expected_output` texts: case 3, under Convert only, and case 14 (a body that updates the current record), which the closing line and Convert Lead teach. Case 3's Bulk half lists `type`, `execution`, `params`, `bulkActions` and `ctx.recordId`, and none of `icon`, `successMessage` or `refreshAfter`: the trimmed block now matches that half key for key.

- N3 (nit) — the copy-holes bullet now names `result` with no word on what it is. The gloss was a hint, not a rule: it stated no constraint and no gate reads it. What still carries the meaning: the worked hole in the same bullet (`resent: 'Invitation resent to {{ result.email }}'`), the `resultDialog` bullet two above it ("shows the server answer", `result.data`, "the whole answer as JSON"), and the Convert Lead `onSuccess` template with its lead-in sentence (`${result.output.opportunity_id}`, an `isOutput` variable). The gloss was also narrower than the contract: the `outcomeMessages` docblock gives `result` as the `target` call's response body on `type: 'api'` and the handler's return value on `type: 'script'`, so "the handler's answer" was exact for a script alone. Residual cost: the file spells `result.data` for `resultDialog` and `result.email` for a copy hole, and the gloss was the one phrase saying the copy-hole `result` is the answer itself; the worked hole still shows the right depth. No eval token rests on it: no `must_contain` holds `handler` or `answer`, and case 8's tokens (`{{`, `onSuccess`, `result.output`) are taught by lines 54, 76 and 101. Nothing untrue is taught. Leave as an accepted deviation, or say it in a few words when the file next has bytes to spare.

- The two "Button Order" sentences: not touched by the delta commit; the prior judgment stands, with N1 an accepted deviation.

- Add to Campaign `icon` and `successMessage`: judged in the prior record as no loss beyond S1; S1 is closed, so nothing of them remains open.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
